citations.quote:
Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]],
[[def-hausdorff-space]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on
$X$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]]); this covers in particular every sheaf
of $k$-vector spaces over a field $k$, which is the case used by the
compact-support calculus, and for such a sheaf the groups below are $k$-vector
spaces and the maps $k$-linear. Global sections are written
$\Gamma(X,-)$ ([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]]). For a compact subset
$K\subseteq X$ ([[def-compact-space]]) let $i:K\hookrightarrow X$ be the
inclusion and consider the canonical restriction map
$$\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F)=(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(K),\qquad s\longmapsto s|_K,$$
which sends a global section ([[def-section-restriction-and-global-section]]) to
the section of the inverse image sheaf ([[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]])
that it induces on $K$. Then $\mathcal F$ is **c-soft**, also **soft for
compact supports**, when this map is surjective for every compact subset
$K\subseteq X$, that is: every section of $\mathcal F$ over a compact subset of
$X$ extends to a global section of $\mathcal F$. For sheaves of abelian groups
$\Gamma_c$ and $H^q_c$ of
[[def-compactly-supported-global-sections]] are the compactly supported
analogues of $\Gamma$ and $H^q$.

Two consistency facts hold; both are immediate from the definitions and from
the extension lemma for sections on a compact set, and they are recorded here
because the compact-support calculus uses the first constantly and the second
for injective sheaves.

1. **Neighbourhood formulation.** By
   [[lem-sections-near-a-compact-set-are-sections-on-that-set]], the target of
   the restriction map is the defining colimit of the
   inverse-image presheaf,
   $(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(K)=\varinjlim_{U\supseteq K}\mathcal F(U)$, so that
   $\mathcal F$ is c-soft if and only if for every compact $K$ and every open
   neighbourhood $U$ of $K$, every section $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ agrees with a
   global section of $\mathcal F$ on some open neighbourhood of $K$. It
   therefore suffices, for c-softness, to test the extended sections only
   locally near $K$.
2. **Flasque implies c-soft.** If $\mathcal F$ is flasque
   ([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) then $\mathcal F$ is c-soft: a class in
   $(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(K)$ is represented by a section $s$ over an open
   neighbourhood $U$ of $K$, and flasqueness extends $s$ to a global section
   $t\in\mathcal F(X)$ with $t|_U=s$, so $t$ is a preimage of that class.

C-softness is a property of the pair $(X,\mathcal F)$ and not of the sheaf
alone: the compact subsets of the base space are part of the test. Nothing is
assumed about the support of the extended global sections, and c-softness is
not the same condition as flasqueness, only implied by it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, and let $X$ be a topological space. Then
$\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ has enough injectives, every abelian sheaf on $X$ admits an
injective resolution ([[def-injective-resolution-in-an-abelian-category]]), and
the embeddings below supply one injective resolution datum
([[def-supplied-injective-resolution-datum]]) on the whole category
$\mathrm{Ab}(X)$: for every abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ the datum assigns one
specific injective resolution
$$0\to\mathcal F\to I^0(\mathcal F)\to I^1(\mathcal F)\to\cdots,$$
built functorially from $\mathcal F$ with no further selection.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a locally
compact Hausdorff space, let $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ be the category of sheaves of
abelian groups on $X$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]]) and let
$$\Gamma(X,-):\mathrm{Ab}(X)\longrightarrow\mathbf{Ab}$$
be the additive left exact global-sections functor
([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]],
[[def-section-restriction-and-global-section]]). For a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on
$X$ define the **compactly supported global sections** of $\mathcal F$ to be the
subgroup
$$\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=\{\,s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F):\operatorname{Supp}(s)\ \text{is a compact subset of }X\,\}\subseteq\Gamma(X,\mathcal F),$$
where the support of a section is the set of points at which its germ is
nonzero ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]], [[def-germ-of-section]],
[[def-compact-space]]). This is a subgroup: the zero section has empty support, negation preserves
support, and the support of a sum is closed in $X$ and contained in the finite
union of the two compact supports, hence compact
([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]],
[[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]).
A morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian
sheaves induces a map $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ by restriction of
$\Gamma(X,\varphi)$, and this makes $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ an additive functor
$\mathrm{Ab}(X)\to\mathbf{Ab}$ ([[def-additive-functor]],
[[def-morphism-of-presheaves]]). Six consistency facts hold; all are immediate
from the definitions, and they record the interface used by the compact-support
calculus.

1. **Well-definedness of $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$.** If $x\notin
   \operatorname{Supp}(s)$ then $s_x=0$ in the stalk $\mathcal F_x$
   ([[def-stalk-of-presheaf]]), and since the stalk maps of a morphism commute
   with the germ maps, $\varphi(s)_x=\varphi_x(s_x)=0$, so
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi(s))\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(s)$. A support
   $\operatorname{Supp}(t)$ is closed in $X$: if $x\notin
   \operatorname{Supp}(t)$ then $t$ agrees with the zero section on some open
   neighbourhood of $x$, by the description of equality of germs
   ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]]). Hence
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi(s))$ is a closed subset of $X$ contained in the
   compact set $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$; being closed in $X$ it is closed in the
   subspace $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$, so it is a compact subset of that compact
   space ([[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]) and therefore
   a compact subset of $X$ ([[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]]), and
   $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ maps $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ into
   $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal G)$. Composites and identities are computed
   componentwise, so $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is a functor; it is additive because
   $\Gamma(X,-)$ is.
2. **Sheaves of $k$-vector spaces.** If $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of
   $k$-vector spaces, then $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ is a $k$-vector subspace of
   $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$: the support of $c\cdot s$ is
   $\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ for $c\ne0$ and $\varnothing$ for $c=0$, and the
   zero section has empty support. For a morphism $\varphi$ of sheaves of
   $k$-vector spaces the map $\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ is $k$-linear, since
   $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ is. The higher derived functors below are computed from
   an injective resolution datum on abelian sheaves, so they are abelian
   groups; the degree-zero part is the $k$-vector space
   $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$.
3. **Left exactness.** For every short exact sequence
   $0\to\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{\varphi'}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal F''\to0$
   of abelian sheaves the sequence
   $$0\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')\xrightarrow{\Gamma_c(\varphi')}\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\Gamma_c(\varphi)}\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F'')$$
   is exact. Injectivity: a monomorphism of sheaves has injective stalk maps
   ([[thm-exactness-of-sheaves-stalkwise]]), so
   $\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi'(s'))=\operatorname{Supp}(s')$ and a section
   killed by $\varphi'$ has all germs zero, hence is zero. Exactness at the
   middle: the kernel of $\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ is the image of
   $\Gamma(X,\varphi')$ by left exactness of global sections
   ([[lem-global-sections-left-exact]]); if $s=\varphi'(s')$ has compact
   support, then $s'$ has the same support,
   $\operatorname{Supp}(s')=\operatorname{Supp}(\varphi'(s'))=
   \operatorname{Supp}(s)$, because $\varphi'$ is stalk-injective, so $s'$ lies
   in $\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')$, and the reverse inclusion is immediate from
   $\varphi\circ\varphi'=0$. Thus $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is an additive left exact
   functor on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ ([[def-left-exact-and-right-exact-functor]]).
4. **The derived functors.** Abelian sheaves on $X$ have enough injectives, and
   the embeddings of [[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]] supply one
   functorial injective resolution datum $\mathcal F\mapsto I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$
   on the whole category $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, under the Axiom of Choice
   ([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]). The
   **compactly supported cohomology** of $\mathcal F$ is
   $$H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=R^q\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F):=H^q\bigl(\Gamma_c(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr)\qquad(q\ge0),\qquad H^q_c(X,\mathcal F):=0\quad(q<0),$$
   the cohomology of the deleted resolution, as in the pattern of
   [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]; for a morphism $\varphi$ we
   write $H^q_c(X,\varphi):=R^q\Gamma_c(X,\varphi)$ for the induced map.
5. **Independence of the datum.** If $J$ is another supplied injective
   resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, then $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$ computed from
   $J$ is naturally isomorphic to $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$ computed from $I$
   ([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]]);
   the Axiom of Dependent Choice needed for that comparison follows from AC
   ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). The notation
   $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)$ therefore does not depend on the datum up to this
   canonical natural isomorphism.
6. **Delta functor and the compact case.** Since $\Gamma_c(X,-)$ is additive
   and left exact and the datum is defined on all of $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$, the
   functors $R^q\Gamma_c(X,-)$, $q\ge0$, carry connecting maps that make them a
   cohomological delta functor with $R^0\Gamma_c(X,-)\cong\Gamma_c(X,-)$, and
   every short exact sequence of abelian sheaves has a long exact
   compact-support cohomology sequence, natural in the sequence
   ([[thm-right-derived-functors-form-a-cohomological-delta-functor]]). If $X$
   is compact, then for every global section $s$ its support is closed in $X$ by
   fact 1, hence a closed subset of the compact space $X$ and therefore
   compact, so every global section is compactly supported; hence
   $\Gamma_c(X,-)=\Gamma(X,-)$ and
   $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)=H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ for every $q$, where $H^q(X,-)$ is
   the sheaf cohomology of [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]
   computed from the same datum.

Assume the Axiom of Dependent Choice.

Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be abelian categories, let $I$ be supplied
injective resolution data on all objects of $\mathcal A$, and let
$F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive left exact functor. Then the additive functors
$$R_I^nF:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B,\qquad n\geq 0,$$
admit connecting maps that make them into a cohomological delta functor on
$\mathcal A$, and $R_I^0F$ is naturally isomorphic to $F$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix a topological space $X$, let
$$\Gamma(X,-):\mathrm{Ab}(X)\to\mathbf{Ab}$$
be the additive left exact global-sections functor
([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]]), and let $I$ be the supplied
functorial injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ of
[[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]]: it assigns to every abelian
sheaf $\mathcal F$ one specific injective resolution
$0\to\mathcal F\to I^\bullet(\mathcal F)$
([[def-right-derived-object-relative-to-injective-resolution-data]]).

For every $q\ge0$ and every abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ define the
**$q$-th sheaf cohomology group of $\mathcal F$** to be the right derived
object of $\Gamma(X,-)$ relative to $I$:
$$H^q(X,\mathcal F):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=H^q\bigl(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet(\mathcal F)_{\mathrm{del}})\bigr),$$
the cohomology object of the complex
$\Gamma(X,I^0(\mathcal F))\to\Gamma(X,I^1(\mathcal F))\to\cdots$ of abelian
groups obtained from the deleted resolution
([[def-deleted-resolution]], [[def-cohomology-object-of-a-cochain-complex]]).
We also set $H^q(X,\mathcal F):=0$ for $q<0$.

Because $I$ is a fixed supplied datum, the group $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ is a
specific group for each pair $(X,\mathcal F)$, and for a morphism
$\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian sheaves we write
$H^q(X,\varphi):=R_I^q\Gamma(X,\varphi)$ for the induced map; it is the map on
cohomology induced by $\Gamma(X,-)$ applied to the cochain maps supplied with
the datum, and it is additive in $\varphi$.

If $J$ is another supplied injective resolution datum on $\mathrm{Ab}(X)$ then
$R_I^q\Gamma(X,-)$ and $R_J^q\Gamma(X,-)$ are naturally isomorphic, so the
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ computed from $J$ agree with the ones above up to a
canonical natural isomorphism; the Axiom of Dependent Choice needed for that
comparison follows from AC
([[thm-right-derived-functors-from-two-supplied-injective-resolution-data-are-naturally-isomorphic]],
[[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]). The notation
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ therefore does not depend on the datum used, up to this
canonical isomorphism, and we call $q$ the **cohomological degree**.

Let $K\subseteq X$ be a compact subset ([[def-compact-space]]) of a locally
compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]),
let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $X$
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]]) and let $i:K\hookrightarrow X$ be the
inclusion. Then the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_{U\supseteq K,\ U\ \text{open}}\mathcal F(U)\longrightarrow\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F)=(i^{-1}\mathcal F)(K)$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups (of $k$-vector spaces when $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces). Moreover, for pairwise disjoint compact
subsets $K_1,\dots,K_m\subseteq X$ and sections $s_j\in\mathcal F(U_j)$ over open
neighbourhoods $U_j$ of the respective $K_j$, there are an open neighbourhood $U$
of $K_1\cup\dots\cup K_m$ and a section $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, together with, for
every $j$, an open neighbourhood $W_j\subseteq U_j$ of $K_j$ with
$s|_{W_j}=s_j|_{W_j}$; in particular the zero section can be prescribed on any
compact set disjoint from the given one. The isomorphism is $k$-linear in the vector-space case, and no
choice principle is used: every selection in the proof is made from finitely
many nonempty sets.

Let $(X, \mathcal{T})$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]). Then:

1. **A neighbourhood base of compact sets.** If $X$ is locally compact
   ([[def-locally-compact-space]]) and Hausdorff ([[def-hausdorff-space]]), then
   every neighbourhood $N$ of a point $x \in X$ ([[def-neighbourhood-top]])
   contains a compact neighbourhood of $x$; so the compact neighbourhoods of $x$
   form a neighbourhood base at $x$.
2. **Heredity along open and closed subspaces.** If $X$ is locally compact and
   Hausdorff and $S \subseteq X$ is open, then the subspace $S$ is locally
   compact ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]). If $X$ is locally compact and
   $F \subseteq X$ is closed, then the subspace $F$ is locally compact; no
   Hausdorff hypothesis is used for this half.
3. **Shrinking inside an open set.** If $X$ is locally compact and Hausdorff,
   $O \subseteq X$ is open and $x \in O$, there is an open $V$ with
   $$x \in V \subseteq \overline{V} \subseteq O$$
   and $\overline{V}$ a compact subset of $X$.
4. **Compact sets sit in open sets with compact closure.** If $X$ is locally
   compact and Hausdorff and $K \subseteq X$ is compact, there is an open
   $V \subseteq X$ with $K \subseteq V$ and $\overline{V}$ a compact subset of
   $X$ ([[def-interior-closure-boundary-top]]).

**No choice principle is used**; every cover produced below is defined by a
formula and thinned by [[lem-compactness-of-a-subspace-is-ambient]], which returns
members rather than indices.

Let $(X, \mathcal{T})$ be a Hausdorff topological space
([[def-hausdorff-space]], [[def-topological-space]]), with compact subsets as in
[[def-compact-space]]. Then:

1. **A point and a disjoint compact set are separated.** If $K \subseteq X$ is
   compact and $x \in X \setminus K$, there are $U, V \in \mathcal{T}$ with
   $$x \in U, \qquad K \subseteq V, \qquad U \cap V = \varnothing .$$
2. **Two disjoint compact sets are separated.** If $K, L \subseteq X$ are compact
   and $K \cap L = \varnothing$, there are $U, V \in \mathcal{T}$ with
   $$L \subseteq U, \qquad K \subseteq V, \qquad U \cap V = \varnothing .$$
3. **Compact implies closed.** Every compact subset of $X$ is closed in $X$.
4. **In a compact Hausdorff space the two classes coincide.** If in addition
   $(X, \mathcal{T})$ is compact, then a subset of $X$ is compact if and only if
   it is closed.

**The proof is written choice-free, and that is not a stylistic preference.** The
textbook argument says "for each $y \in K$ choose disjoint open $U_y, V_y$",
which is a selection over an arbitrary index set and therefore an appeal to the
full Axiom of Choice. What is done below instead is to take the family of **all**
open $V$ that admit some open $U \ni x$ disjoint from them — a family cut out by
a formula, with nothing selected — extract a finite subcover from it, and only
then make finitely many selections, which [[lem-finite-choice]] supplies as a
theorem of ZF.

Let $(X, \mathcal{T})$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]), with
subspaces as in [[def-subspace-topology-top]] and compactness as in
[[def-compact-space]]. Then:

1. **Closed in compact is compact.** If $(X, \mathcal{T})$ is compact and
   $F \subseteq X$ is closed in $X$, then $F$ is a compact subset of $X$.
2. **Finite unions.** If $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $K_0, \dots, K_n$ are compact
   subsets of $X$, then $K_0 \cup \dots \cup K_n$ is a compact subset of $X$. The
   union of the empty list is $\varnothing$, which is a compact subset of every
   space.

Claim 1 needs $X$ to be compact and claim 2 does not; no hypothesis of any kind
is placed on $X$ in claim 2. **No choice principle is used**: claim 1 selects
nothing, taking a least index where a selection would be natural, and claim 2
makes finitely many selections through [[lem-finite-choice]], a theorem of ZF.

Let $(X, \mathcal{T})$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]), let
$A \subseteq X$ and let $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ be the subspace
([[def-subspace-topology-top]]). Then:

1. **Compactness read in the ambient space.** $A$ is a compact subset of $X$
   ([[def-compact-space]]), that is $(A, \mathcal{T}_A)$ is a compact space, if
   and only if for every family $\mathcal{U} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ with
   $A \subseteq \bigcup \mathcal{U}$ there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and
   $U_0, \dots, U_n \in \mathcal{U}$ with $A \subseteq U_0 \cup \dots \cup U_n$,
   or else $A = \varnothing$.
2. **The same in indexed form.** $A$ is a compact subset of $X$ if and only if
   for every set $I$ and every family $(U_i)_{i \in I}$ of open subsets of $X$
   with $A \subseteq \bigcup_{i \in I} U_i$ there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and
   indices $i_0, \dots, i_n \in I$ with
   $A \subseteq U_{i_0} \cup \dots \cup U_{i_n}$, or else $A = \varnothing$.

Claim 2 is the form used by almost every later proof on this page, because a
cover is usually produced by a rule that attaches an open set to each point or to
each index, and a set of open sets forgets that rule. No choice principle is used
anywhere below; the one place a selection is made is over a finite index set, and
[[lem-finite-choice]] is a theorem of ZF.

Let $X$ be a compact ([[def-compact-space]]) Hausdorff
([[def-hausdorff-space]]) topological space. Then:

1. $X$ is **regular** ([[def-regular-and-t3-spaces]]);
2. $X$ is **normal** ([[def-normal-and-t4-spaces]]);
3. $X$ is $T_1$ ([[def-t0-and-t1-spaces]]), and hence $X$ is $T_3$ and $T_4$.

Following [[def-regular-and-t3-spaces]] and [[def-normal-and-t4-spaces]],
*regular* and *normal* name the separation conditions alone and the numerals
$T_3$ and $T_4$ name their conjunctions with $T_1$; claim 3 is what supplies the
$T_1$ half, and it is stated separately for that reason.

**Nothing stronger is claimed.** In particular it is not asserted here that a
compact Hausdorff space is completely regular
([[def-regular-and-t3-spaces]] distinguishes the two conditions), and no
continuous real-valued function is produced anywhere below.

Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on a topological space $X$. We say that
$\mathcal F$ is a **sheaf** if for every open set $U \subseteq X$ and every
open cover $U=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$, including the empty cover of
$\varnothing$, the following two conditions hold.

**Locality.** If $s,t\in\mathcal F(U)$ satisfy
$$s|_{U_i}=t|_{U_i}\qquad\text{for all }i\in I,$$
then $s=t$.

**Gluing.** If sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ satisfy
$$s_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=s_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}\qquad\text{for all }i,j\in I,$$
then there exists $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that
$$s|_{U_i}=s_i\qquad\text{for all }i\in I.$$

By locality, such a section $s$ is automatically unique. Thus a sheaf is
exactly a presheaf whose compatible local sections glue uniquely.

Let
$$
\cdots\longrightarrow \mathcal F_{i-1}\xrightarrow{d_{i-1}}\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{d_i}\mathcal F_{i+1}\longrightarrow\cdots
$$
be a sequence of sheaves of abelian groups on a topological space $X$. Then the
sequence is exact if and only if, for every point $x\in X$, the stalk sequence
$$
\cdots\longrightarrow (\mathcal F_{i-1})_x\xrightarrow{(d_{i-1})_x}(\mathcal F_i)_x\xrightarrow{(d_i)_x}(\mathcal F_{i+1})_x\longrightarrow\cdots
$$
is exact.

Let $X$ be a topological space. If
$$
0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''
$$
is exact in sheaves of abelian groups on $X$, then
$$
0\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F')\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F'')
$$
is exact. However, there exists an epimorphism of sheaves of abelian groups on
some space $X$ whose induced map on global sections is not surjective.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf on $Y$, and let
$x\in X$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x\cong \mathcal G_{f(x)}.
$$

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $U$.

For an open set $V \subseteq X$, define
$$(j_!\mathcal F)(V) := \left\{ s\in \mathcal F(V\cap U): \operatorname{Supp}(s)\text{ is closed in }V \right\}.$$
Equivalently, $s$ lies in $(j_!\mathcal F)(V)$ exactly when for every
$x\in V\setminus U$ there exists an open neighbourhood $W_x \subseteq V$ with
$$
s|_{W_x\cap U}=0.
$$

Restriction maps are inherited from $\mathcal F$, so $j_!\mathcal F$ is a
subsheaf of $j_*\mathcal F$. When $V \subseteq U$, the support condition is
vacuous and
$$
(j_!\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V).
$$

This is the **extension by zero** of $\mathcal F$ along $j$. It is distinct in
general from the ordinary direct image $j_*\mathcal F$.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace.

1. For every sheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal F$ on $U$ and every sheaf of
   abelian groups $\mathcal G$ on $X$, there is a natural bijection
   $$\operatorname{Hom}_X(j_!\mathcal F,\mathcal G) \cong \operatorname{Hom}_U(\mathcal F,j^{-1}\mathcal G).$$
2. The functor $j_!$ is exact on sheaves of abelian groups.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of an open subspace
([[def-topological-space]]) with closed complement $Z=X\setminus U$, let
$i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of the subspace
([[def-subspace-topology-top]]), and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups
on $X$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]).
Write $\mathcal F|_U:=j^{-1}\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal F|_Z:=i^{-1}\mathcal F$ for
the restrictions ([[def-restriction-sheaf-open-subspace]]). Then:

1. the adjoint transpose of the identity of $\mathcal F|_U$ under the adjunction
   of [[thm-extension-by-zero-adjunction-exactness]] and the unit of the
   adjunction ([[thm-inverse-direct-image-adjunction]]) fit into a short exact
   sequence of sheaves of abelian groups on $X$
   $$0\to j_!(\mathcal F|_U)\to\mathcal F\to i_*(\mathcal F|_Z)\to0,$$
   where $j_!$ is extension by zero ([[def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf]]) and
   $i_*$ is the direct image ([[def-direct-image-sheaf]],
   [[lem-direct-image-is-sheaf]]); exactness is that of
   [[def-exact-sequence-sheaves]];
2. if $\mathcal F=\mathbb Z_X$ is the constant sheaf with value $\mathbb Z$ on
   $X$, then $\mathcal F|_U$ is canonically isomorphic to the constant sheaf
   $\mathbb Z_U$ on $U$, so the sequence of clause 1 reads
   $0\to j_!(\mathbb Z_U)\to\mathbb Z_X\to i_*(\mathcal F|_Z)\to0$ up to that
   canonical isomorphism.

Let $X$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]). Let
$\mathbb Z_{\mathrm{pt}}$ be the constant presheaf with value $\mathbb Z$,
let
$$\mathbb Z_X:=a\,\mathbb Z_{\mathrm{pt}}$$
be its sheafification with sheafification map
$\eta:\mathbb Z_{\mathrm{pt}}\to\mathbb Z_X$, and put
$$1_X:=\eta_X(1)\in\Gamma(X,\mathbb Z_X),$$
where $1\in\mathbb Z_{\mathrm{pt}}(X)=\mathbb Z$
([[lem-constant-sheaf-is-the-sheaf-of-locally-constant-functions]],
[[def-sheafification]]). For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ let
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ab}(X)}(\mathbb Z_X,\mathcal F)$ be the abelian
group of morphisms of sheaves of abelian groups, with addition computed
componentwise ([[def-global-sections-functor-sheaves]],
[[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]). Then:

1. **(Sections as morphisms.)** For every abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ the map
   $$\Phi_{\mathcal F}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ab}(X)}(\mathbb Z_X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow\Gamma(X,\mathcal F),\qquad \varphi\mapsto\varphi_X(1_X),$$
   is a bijection. Its inverse sends $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ to the unique
   morphism of sheaves $\varphi:\mathbb Z_X\to\mathcal F$ with
   $\varphi_X(1_X)=s$, and that morphism is described as follows: for every open
   $U\subseteq X$, every locally constant $f:U\to\mathbb Z$ and every
   $n\in\mathbb Z$ one has
   $$\varphi_U(f)|_{f^{-1}(n)}=n\cdot s|_{f^{-1}(n)},$$
   the pair $\mathbb Z_X(U)\cong\{f:U\to\mathbb Z\text{ locally constant}\}$
   being the identification of clause 2 of
   [[lem-constant-sheaf-is-the-sheaf-of-locally-constant-functions]].

2. **(Additivity and naturality.)** $\Phi_{\mathcal F}$ is a homomorphism of
   abelian groups for every $\mathcal F$, hence an isomorphism, and for every
   morphism $\psi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of abelian sheaves one has
   $$\Phi_{\mathcal G}(\psi\circ\varphi)=\Gamma(X,\psi)\bigl(\Phi_{\mathcal F}(\varphi)\bigr)$$
   for all $\varphi:\mathbb Z_X\to\mathcal F$; thus the bijections
   $\Phi_{\mathcal F}$ are natural in $\mathcal F$.

3. **(Complexes.)** If $J^\bullet$ is a cochain complex of abelian sheaves
   ([[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]]) and $\mathbb Z_X$ is read
   as the stalk complex concentrated in degree $0$
   ([[def-zero-and-stalk-complex]]), then the levelwise maps
   $\Phi_{J^n}$ define an isomorphism of cochain complexes
   ([[def-cochain-map]])
   $$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}^\bullet(\mathbb Z_X,J^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\Gamma(X,J^\bullet),$$
   where the left-hand complex is the cochain Hom complex
   ([[def-homotopically-projective-bounded-above-complex]]), the right-hand
   complex has the differentials $\Gamma(X,d^n)$ and entries
   $\Gamma(X,J^n)$, and the isomorphism is natural in the complex
   $J^\bullet$.

An object $I$ of an abelian category is **injective** when for every monomorphism
$m:M\rightarrowtail E$ and every morphism $f:M\to I$, there exists a morphism
$\widetilde f:E\to I$ with

$$\widetilde f\,m=f.$$

The extension $\widetilde f$ need not be unique.

Let $X$ be a topological space and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian
groups on $X$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]). For open subsets
$U\subseteq V\subseteq X$ write
$$\rho^V_U:\mathcal F(V)\longrightarrow\mathcal F(U)$$
for the restriction map of $\mathcal F$
([[def-section-restriction-and-global-section]]).

Then $\mathcal F$ is **flasque**, also called **flabby**, when each of these
restriction maps is surjective: for all open $U\subseteq V\subseteq X$ the map
$\rho^V_U$ is onto. Equivalently, $\mathcal F$ is flasque when every section of
$\mathcal F$ over an open subset $U$ extends to every larger open subset $V$,
that is, when for every $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ there is $t\in\mathcal F(V)$ with
$t|_U=s$.

The same condition on restriction maps defines flasque sheaves of sets and
flasque sheaves of modules over a sheaf of rings; on this page the notion is
used for sheaves of abelian groups.

Let $R$ be a unital ring and $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ a family of left $R$-modules ([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). Their **direct product** is the module $\prod_{i\in I}M_i$ with coordinatewise operations. The **support** of $m=(m_i)$ is $\{i\in I:m_i\ne0\}$, and the **direct sum** is the submodule
$$\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i=\{m\in\prod_{i\in I}M_i:\operatorname{supp}(m)\text{ is finite}\}$$
([[def-submodule]]).

This subset is a submodule because the support of a sum is contained in the union of two finite supports and scalar multiplication cannot enlarge support.

For each $i$, the coordinate inclusion $\jmath_i:M_i\to\bigoplus_jM_j$ puts its input in coordinate $i$ and zero elsewhere. If $I=\varnothing$, both product and direct sum are the zero module.

Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be
$\mathcal O_X$-modules, and let $x\in X$. Then there is a canonical
isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules
$$(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)_x \cong \mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal G_x.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be
$\mathcal O_X$-modules. The **tensor-product presheaf**
$$
\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G
$$
is defined by
$$(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)(U) := \mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal G(U)$$
for each open set $U \subseteq X$, with restriction induced from the
restriction maps of $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$.

The **tensor-product sheaf** is the sheafification of this presheaf:
$$\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G := a(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G).$$

**Assume the Axiom of Choice** ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), which is what
[[thm-zorn]] is proved from. Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $F$
([[def-vector-space]]) and let $L \subseteq S \subseteq V$ with $L$ linearly
independent ([[def-linear-independence]]) and $\operatorname{span}(S) = V$
([[def-linear-combination-and-span]]). Then there is a basis $B$ of $V$
([[def-linear-basis]]) with

$$L \;\subseteq\; B \;\subseteq\; S .$$

Let $X$ be a topological space ([[def-topological-space]]) and let $A$ be a
set. A function $f:U\to A$ on an open subset $U\subseteq X$ is **locally
constant** when every $x\in U$ has an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ with
$x\in V$ on which $f$ is constant. Let $A_{\mathrm{pt}}$ be the **constant
presheaf** with value $A$, $A_{\mathrm{pt}}(U)=A$ for every open $U$ with all
restriction maps the identity ([[def-presheaf-on-topological-space]]), and let
$$A_X:=aA_{\mathrm{pt}}$$
be its sheafification ([[def-sheafification]]), the **constant sheaf** with
value $A$ on $X$. Then:

1. the assignment $\underline A_{\mathrm{loc}}(U):=\{f:U\to A\text{ locally
   constant}\}$, with the usual restriction maps, is a sheaf of sets on $X$, and
   for every $x\in X$ evaluation at $x$ is a canonical bijection
   $\underline A_{\mathrm{loc},x}\cong A$
   ([[lem-locally-constant-functions-form-a-sheaf]]);
2. there is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves of sets
   $$\theta:A_X\longrightarrow\underline A_{\mathrm{loc}}$$
   such that for every open $U\subseteq X$ and every $a\in A$ the section
   $\theta_U(\eta_{U}(a))$ is the constant function with value $a$, where
   $\eta:A_{\mathrm{pt}}\to A_X$ is the sheafification map;
3. if $A$ is an abelian group, then $A_{\mathrm{pt}}$ with its group operation is
   a presheaf of abelian groups ([[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]]) and
   $\underline A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ with pointwise addition is a sheaf of abelian
   groups ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]); the maps
   $a\mapsto\text{the constant function with value }a$ are group homomorphisms,
   and the group structures transported along the bijections $\theta_U$ make
   $A_X$ a sheaf of abelian groups for which every $\eta_U$ and every $\theta_U$
   is a group homomorphism.

Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of sheaves of sets on a
topological space $X$. Then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism if and only if, for
every $x\in X$, the induced map on stalks
$$\varphi_x:\mathcal F_x\longrightarrow\mathcal G_x$$
is a bijection.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $F$ be a function with domain $n$ all of whose
values are nonempty sets. Then the family of its values,
$\mathcal{F} = F[n] = \{\, F(i) : i \in n \,\}$, has a choice function
([[def-choice-function]]).

This is a theorem of ZF: its proof uses no form of the Axiom of Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

What is proved below is exactly the displayed statement, by induction on $n$. The
natural number $n$ serves as the index set in the von Neumann sense,
$n = \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), so "$F$ has domain $n$"
says precisely that the members of $\mathcal{F}$ are listed as
$F(0), \dots, F(n-1)$. The listing need not be injective, and $\mathcal{F}$ is the
set of values, so repetitions are harmless and are not counted.

The displayed statement and its proof use only a natural-number-indexed
function. They do not identify an arbitrary finite family with a particular
enumeration.

derivations.claim: Let $C_1,C_2\subseteq X$ be compact, let $V_1,V_2$ be open with $C_k\subseteq V_k$, let $s_k\in\mathcal F(V_k)$, and suppose that $W\subseteq V_1\cap V_2$ is open with $C_1\cap C_2\subseteq W$ and $s_1|_W=s_2|_W$. Then there are an open $V\supseteq C_1\cup C_2$ and $s\in\mathcal F(V)$ with $s=s_k$ on an open neighbourhood of $C_k$ for $k=1,2$: the sets $A:=C_1\setminus W$ and $B:=C_2\setminus W$ are compact and disjoint ([F3]), hence separated by disjoint open $G_1\supseteq A$, $G_2\supseteq B$ ([F3]); with $V_k':=V_k\cap(G_k\cup W)$ one has $C_k\subseteq V_k'$, $V_1'\cap V_2'\subseteq W$, so $s_1|_{V_1'}$ and $s_2|_{V_2'}$ glue to the required $s$ over $V_1'\cup V_2'\supseteq C_1\cup C_2$ ([F4]).

Let $C\subseteq X$ be compact, $B\subseteq X$ closed, $V\subseteq X$ open with $C\cup B\subseteq V$, $s_C\in\mathcal F(V)$ and $s_B\in\mathcal F(V)$ with $s_C|_W=s_B|_W$ for an open $W\subseteq V$ containing $C\cap B$. Then there are an open $V_0\subseteq V$ with $C\cup B\subseteq V_0$ and $s_0\in\mathcal F(V_0)$ with $s_0=s_C$ on an open neighbourhood of $C$ and $s_0=s_B$ on an open neighbourhood of $B$. Indeed $A:=C\setminus W$ is compact, $B_0:=B\setminus W$ is closed, and $A\cap B_0=\varnothing$; covering $A$ by finitely many open $V_x$ with $x\in V_x\subseteq\overline{V_x}\subseteq X\setminus B_0$ and $\overline{V_x}$ compact ([F3]) and setting $G_1:=\bigcup V_x\supseteq A$, $G_2:=X\setminus\bigcup\overline{V_x}\supseteq B\setminus W$ one has $G_1\cap G_2=\varnothing$; now $V_0':=V\cap(G_1\cup W)$ contains $C$, $V_0'':=V\cap(G_2\cup W)$ contains $B$, and $V_0'\cap V_0''\subseteq W$, so the restrictions of $s_C$ and $s_B$ glue ([F3, F4]).

**Clause (1).** Let $\mathcal F$ be c-soft, let $K\subseteq X$ be compact and let $W\subseteq X$ be an open neighbourhood of $K$; let $\sigma\in\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F)$ be represented by $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ for an open $U\supseteq K$ ([F2]), and replace $U$ by $U\cap W$. Choose open $W_0,W_1$ with $K\subseteq W_0\subseteq\overline{W_0}\subseteq W_1\subseteq\overline{W_1}\subseteq W$ and $\overline{W_1}$ compact (finitely many applications of the shrinking of [F3]); put $C:=\overline{W_1}\setminus W_0$, a compact set disjoint from $K$. Since $\mathcal F$ is c-soft, $[s]\in\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F)$ has a preimage $t_1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ ([F1]); by [F2] $t_1=s$ on an open neighbourhood of $K$. Apply the gluing of [F2] to the disjoint compact sets $K$ and $C$ with the sections $t_1$ (over $X$) and $0$ (over $X$): there are an open $V\supseteq K\cup C$ and $u\in\mathcal F(V)$ with $u=t_1$ on an open neighbourhood of $K$ and $u=0$ on an open neighbourhood of $C$. Choose a compact $K'$ with $K\cup C\subseteq K'\subseteq V$ ([F3]) and extend the class of $u|_{K'}$ to a global section $t_2\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ by c-softness ([F1]); then $t_2=u$ on an open neighbourhood of $K'$ by [F2]. Finally $t_2=0$ on the open set $W_1\setminus\overline{W_0}$: it is contained in $C\subseteq K'$ and $u=0$ near $C$; hence $t_2|_{W_1}$ and $0$ agree on $W_1\setminus\overline{W_0}$ and glue across the open cover $\{W_1,X\setminus\overline{W_0}\}$ of $X$ to a section $t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ with $t=t_2$ on $W_1$ and $t=0$ on $X\setminus\overline{W_0}$ ([F4]). Then $\operatorname{Supp}(t)\subseteq\overline{W_0}\subseteq W$, so $t$ is compactly supported with support inside the prescribed $W$, and $t=t_2=t_1=s$ near $K$, so $t$ represents $\sigma$ over $K$.

**Clause (2).** Let $\mathcal I$ be an injective abelian sheaf and let $U\subseteq X$ be open. By [F5] the canonical map $j_!\mathbb Z_U\to\mathbb Z_X$ is a monomorphism, so injectivity of $\mathcal I$ makes $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z_X,\mathcal I)\to\operatorname{Hom}(j_!\mathbb Z_U,\mathcal I)$ surjective; under the adjunction and the identifications of [F5], $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb Z_X,\mathcal I)\cong\Gamma(X,\mathcal I)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!\mathbb Z_U,\mathcal I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_U(\mathbb Z_U,\mathcal I|_U)\cong\Gamma(U,\mathcal I)$, and the composite is the restriction map. Hence every section of $\mathcal I$ over an open set extends to $X$, that is, $\mathcal I$ is flasque, and a flasque sheaf is c-soft by [F1].

**Lifting over a compact space.** Let $Y$ be a compact Hausdorff space, let $0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\xrightarrow{\gamma}\mathcal C\to0$ be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $Y$ with $\mathcal A$ c-soft on $Y$, and let $c\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal C)$. Then $c$ has a preimage in $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal B)$. Indeed, the family of all pairs $(U,b)$ with $U\subseteq Y$ open, $b\in\mathcal B(U)$ and $\gamma_U(b)=c|_U$ is cut out by a formula and covers $Y$ (the stalk maps of $\gamma$ are onto, [F4]); by compactness and normality of $Y$ ([F3]) there are finitely many compact $K_1,\dots,K_m$ covering $Y$ with lifts $b_i\in\mathcal B(V_i)$ over open $V_i\supseteq K_i$. We show by induction on $m$ that the pieces can be corrected, without changing their images under $\gamma$, so that they agree near all pairwise intersections and glue ([F2]); for $m=1$ there is nothing to do. For $m\ge2$, the induction hypothesis gives a section $b'$ over an open neighbourhood of $D:=K_1\cup\dots\cup K_{m-1}$ with $\gamma(b')=c$ there; over an open neighbourhood of the compact set $D\cap K_m$ the difference $b'-b_m$ has vanishing $\gamma$, so it lies in the image of $\mathcal A$ ([F4]); the corresponding section of $\mathcal A$ over that neighbourhood extends to $Y$ by c-softness of $\mathcal A$, and adding its image to $b_m$ keeps $\gamma(b_m)=c$ while making $b'-b_m$ vanish near $D\cap K_m$; the gluing of step 1.1 applied to the compact pieces $D$ and $K_m$ then produces a section over an open neighbourhood of $D\cup K_m$ mapping to $c$, completing the induction. Since $K_1\cup\dots\cup K_m=Y$ and a neighbourhood of $Y$ in $Y$ is $Y$, this is a preimage of $c$ in $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal B)$.

**Clause (4), the topological preservations.** Let $\mathcal F$ be c-soft. (i) For an open subspace $U\subseteq X$: a compact subset of $U$ is compact in $X$ ([F3]) and a section of $\mathcal F|_U$ over it is represented by an ambient section over a neighbourhood, which clause (1) extends with support control into any prescribed neighbourhood; restricting the result to $U$ extends the given section, so $\mathcal F|_U$ is c-soft. (ii) For a closed subspace $Z\subseteq X$: compact subsets of $Z$ are compact in $X$ ([F3]) and a section of $\mathcal F|_Z$ over one is a class of ambient sections over neighbourhoods of it in $X$ ([F2]); clause (1) extends such a class, and restricting to $Z$ gives the required extension, so $\mathcal F|_Z$ is c-soft. (iii) Let $\mathcal A$ be any c-soft sheaf on the open subspace $U$, which is locally compact Hausdorff by [F3], and put $\mathcal G:=j_!\mathcal A$. Its stalks are $\mathcal A_x$ on $U$ and zero outside $U$, by the local support condition of [F5]. Let $K\subseteq X$ be compact and represent a section over it by $s\in\mathcal G(V)$, $V\supseteq K$ open [F2]. The set $L:=K\cap\operatorname{Supp}(s)$ is closed in $K$, hence compact, and lies in $V\cap U$. If $L=\varnothing$, the zero global section has the required germs on $K$. Otherwise choose opens $W_0,W_1$ with $L\subseteq W_0\subseteq\overline{W_0}\subseteq W_1\subseteq\overline{W_1}\subseteq V\cap U$ and compact closures [F3]. In $U$ the sets $T:=K\cap\overline{W_1}$ and $C:=\overline{W_1}\setminus W_0$ are compact. The class of $s$ on $T$ and the zero class on $C$ agree on $T\cap C$, since every such point belongs to $K\setminus L$ and has zero germ of $s$. By the fusion of step 1.1 and the neighbourhood representation of [F2], they give a section near $T\cup C$ in $U$. C-softness of $\mathcal A$ extends this class to $g\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal A)$, agreeing with $s$ near $T$ and with zero near $C$. Glue $g|_{W_1}$ with zero on $U\setminus\overline{W_0}$; the overlap lies in $C$. The result $e\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal A)$ has support closed and contained in the compact $\overline{W_0}\subseteq U$, hence lies in $\Gamma_c(X,j_!\mathcal A)$. On $K\cap W_1$ it has the germs of $s$, and on $K\setminus\overline{W_0}$ both germs vanish because $L\subseteq W_0$. Thus $e$ represents the original section over $K$, proving c-softness of $j_!\mathcal A$.

**Clause (4), finite sums and constant-vector tensors.** For a finite family of c-soft abelian sheaves, sections of the direct sum are finite tuples of sections: componentwise locality and gluing show that the finite product presheaf is a sheaf, and the finite product is also the direct sum. A class over a compact $K$ is represented by a tuple on a neighbourhood of $K$ [F2]; extend each component by step 1.3 and form the tuple of global sections. This proves c-softness of finite direct sums. Now assume $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of $k$-vector spaces, let $M$ be any $k$-vector space and $\mathcal H:=\mathcal F\otimes_{k_X}M_X$. Choose a basis $B$ of $M$ under AC [F6, F7]. Each coordinate functional $\lambda_b:M\to k$ induces a sheaf morphism $\mathcal H\to\mathcal F$ via $\mathrm{id}\otimes(\lambda_b)_X$ and the canonical $\mathcal F\otimes_{k_X}k_X\cong\mathcal F$; the latter map is multiplication and is an isomorphism on stalks [F6]. A germ of $\mathcal H$ is a finite sum of $\mathcal F$-germs times basis vectors, by [F6]. Represent its coefficients by local sections; equality of germs gives the same finite-sum expression on a smaller neighbourhood. Thus a section $s$ representing a class over compact $K$ has finite coordinate expressions locally near $K$. Compactness gives finitely many such neighbourhoods, whose union $O$ contains $K$ and whose expressions use one finite subset $B_0\subseteq B$. Put $s_b:=(\mathrm{id}\otimes\lambda_b)(s|_O)$ for $b\in B_0$; uniqueness of basis coordinates and locality give $s|_O=\sum_{b\in B_0}s_b\otimes b$. Extend the finitely many $s_b$ to global sections $t_b$ agreeing near $K$ by step 1.3. Then $\sum_{b\in B_0}t_b\otimes b$ is a global section of $\mathcal H$ agreeing with $s$ near $K$. The zero-coefficient case $M=0$ is immediate. This proves the tensor clause for arbitrary constant $M$.

**Clause (5), local lifting.** Let $\mathcal F'$ be c-soft, let $K\subseteq X$ be compact and let $\sigma''\in\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F'')$ be represented by a section $s''\in\mathcal F''(U)$ over an open $U\supseteq K$ ([F2]). Choose open $U_0$ with $K\subseteq U_0\subseteq\overline{U_0}\subseteq U$ and $\overline{U_0}$ compact ([F3]). The restricted sheaves on the compact space $\overline{U_0}$ form a short exact sequence whose kernel is c-soft on $\overline{U_0}$: a compact subset of $\overline{U_0}$ is compact in $X$ ([F3]) and a section of the restricted kernel over it is represented by an ambient section of $\mathcal F'$ over an open neighbourhood ([F2]), which c-softness of $\mathcal F'$ extends to $X$. Hence the lifting lemma of step 2.1 applies to the compact space $\overline{U_0}$ and the class of $s''$ over it: there is $t\in\Gamma(\overline{U_0},i^{-1}\mathcal F)$ with $\beta(t)$ equal to that class. Represent $t$ by a section of $\mathcal F$ over an open $V\supseteq\overline{U_0}$ ([F2]); shrinking $V$ we may assume that the image of that section under $\beta$ equals $s''$ on $V$ (they agree as classes over $\overline{U_0}$, hence near it, [F2]). This section of $\mathcal F$ over the open neighbourhood $V$ of $K$ lifts the given class $\sigma''$; since $K$ and $\sigma''$ were arbitrary, clause (5) holds locally.

**Clause (5), compact-support exactness.** Let $\mathcal F'$ be c-soft; we show that $\Gamma_c(\beta):\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F'')$ is surjective. Let $s''\in\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F'')$ and put $S:=\operatorname{Supp}(s'')$, compact. Choose open $W_0,W_1$ with $S\subseteq W_0\subseteq\overline{W_0}\subseteq W_1\subseteq\overline{W_1}$ and $\overline{W_1}$ compact (finitely many shrinkings, [F3]); put $C:=\overline{W_1}\setminus W_0$, a compact set disjoint from $S$. Apply the lifting lemma of step 2.1 to the compact space $\overline{W_1}$ and the class of $s''$ over it: there is $t\in\Gamma(\overline{W_1},i^{-1}\mathcal F)$ with $\beta(t)=s''|_{\overline{W_1}}$; represent $t$ by $a\in\mathcal F(V_0)$ over an open $V_0\supseteq\overline{W_1}$ with $\beta(a)=s''|_{V_0}$ ([F2]). On the open set $O:=V_0\setminus S$ the section $a$ has $\beta(a)=s''=0$, hence $a|_O=\alpha(e)$ for a uniquely determined $e\in\mathcal F'(O)$: the family of all open $O_x\subseteq V_0$ over which $a$ lies in the image of $\alpha$ covers $V_0\setminus S$ ([F4], the kernel of $\beta$ is the image of $\alpha$ as subsheaves) and the local sections glue because $\alpha$ is injective on sections ([F4]). The compact set $C=\overline{W_1}\setminus W_0$ is contained in $O$, so $e$ is a section of the c-soft $\mathcal F'$ over an open neighbourhood of the compact set $C$; by clause (1) applied to $\mathcal F'$ there is $e_X\in\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F')$ with $e_X=e$ near $C$ ([F2]). Set $a_1:=a-\alpha(e_X)|_{V_0}\in\mathcal F(V_0)$: then $\beta(a_1)=s''|_{V_0}$, and $a_1$ vanishes on the open set $O_C:=\{\,x\in V_0: a_x=\alpha(e_X)_x\,\}$, which contains $C$. The overlap $W_1\setminus\overline{W_0}$ of the open cover $\{W_1,X\setminus\overline{W_0}\}$ of $X$ is contained in $C\subseteq O_C$, where $a_1$ vanishes, so $a_1|_{W_1}$ and the zero section on $X\setminus\overline{W_0}$ agree there and glue to a section $t'\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ with $t'=a_1$ on $W_1$ and $t'=0$ on $X\setminus\overline{W_0}$ ([F4]). Then $\operatorname{Supp}(t')\subseteq\overline{W_0}$ is compact, and $\beta(t')=s''$: on $W_1$ one has $\beta(a_1)=s''$, while on $X\setminus\overline{W_0}$ both sides vanish since $S\subseteq W_0\subseteq\overline{W_0}$, and $W_1\cup(X\setminus\overline{W_0})=X$. Therefore $t'\in\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ with $\Gamma_c(\beta)(t')=s''$.

**Clause (5), quotient.** Let $\mathcal F'$ and $\mathcal F$ be c-soft. Let $K\subseteq X$ be compact and let $\sigma''\in\Gamma(K,i^{-1}\mathcal F'')$: by step 3.1 it is lifted by a section $u$ of $\mathcal F$ over an open neighbourhood of $K$, and clause (1) applied to the c-soft $\mathcal F$ with the compact set $K$ and the prescribed neighbourhood of $u$ produces $t\in\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)$ with $t=u$ near $K$; then $\beta(t)\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F'')$ restricts to $\sigma''$ over $K$, so every class over a compact set extends to a global section and $\mathcal F''$ is c-soft.

**Clause (3).** Let $\mathcal F$ be c-soft and resolve it by injectives, $0\to\mathcal F\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$, using the functorial datum of [F1]; each $I^j$ is c-soft by clause (2) ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-have-enough-injectives]] supplies the resolution terms as injective objects). The syzygies $Z^0:=\mathcal F$, $Z^{j+1}:=\operatorname{im}(I^j\to I^{j+1})$ are c-soft: $Z^1=\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal F\to I^0)$ is a quotient of c-soft sheaves in $0\to\mathcal F\to I^0\to Z^1\to0$, and inductively $Z^{j+1}$ is a quotient of c-soft sheaves in $0\to Z^j\to I^j\to Z^{j+1}\to0$ (clause (5)); hence each short exact sequence $0\to Z^j\to I^j\to Z^{j+1}\to0$ consists of c-soft sheaves, so by clause (5) the sequence $0\to\Gamma_c(X,Z^j)\to\Gamma_c(X,I^j)\to\Gamma_c(X,Z^{j+1})\to0$ is exact. Therefore the augmented complex $0\to\Gamma_c(X,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma_c(X,I^0)\to\Gamma_c(X,I^1)\to\cdots$ is exact, and $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)=H^q(\Gamma_c(X,I^\bullet_{\mathrm{del}}))=0$ for $q>0$ ([F1]). For $X$ compact the identification $H^q_c(X,\mathcal F)=H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ of [F1] gives the vanishing of sheaf cohomology.

**Conclusion.** Clause (1) is step 1.3, clause (2) is step 1.4, clause (3) is step 5.1, clause (4) is steps 2.2 and 2.3, and clause (5) is steps 3.1, 3.2 and 4.1. The Axiom of Choice supplies the coefficient basis of step 2.3 and the injective resolution datum and derived-functor statements of [F1]; all topological selections are finite.

boundaries.evidence: A section over the empty compact set is the zero section and extends trivially, so the extension assertions of steps 1.3, 3.1 and 3.2 are vacuous there, and step 4.1 applies to the zero class.
The zero sheaf is flasque and c-soft and its compactly supported sections vanish; steps 1.3, 3.1 and 5.1 apply verbatim with all sections equal to 0.

boundaries.reason: No multiplicative-unit or singleton-index hypothesis is used; the direct-sum clause of step 2.3 is stated for an arbitrary finite family of c-soft sheaves.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.3 treats the case of a section supported in a prescribed neighbourhood and step 1.4 the case of an injective sheaf; the degenerate case K=X of a compact space is covered because a neighbourhood of X is X in step 2.1.

boundaries.reason: There is no interval or ordered parameter; the vanishing statement of step 5.1 begins at q>0, the case q=0 being the definition of Gamma_c.

boundaries.evidence: AC is used to choose a basis for arbitrary constant-vector coefficients in step 2.3 and for the supplied injective/derived data. Compact-set patching uses finite selections.

boundaries.reason: The Statement gives one-way implications and canonical isomorphisms, rather than a c-softness/acyclicity biconditional. The converse criterion is a separate lemma.
The Statement gives one-way implications and canonical isomorphisms, rather than a c-softness/acyclicity biconditional. The converse criterion is a separate lemma.

risk_review.notes: All twelve steps and all 34 original prerequisites independently read. Schapira pp.207–209 were read through the relevant complete displayed proofs (some source results are exercises or deferred); Stacks 09SX and its entire 01EA proof independently checked. Compact annuli provide controlled support, the corrected plus sign makes compact lifts agree, c-soft kernel gives compact-section surjectivity without assuming the middle term c-soft, quotient closure makes all injective-resolution syzygies c-soft, and compact sections then form an exact augmented complex. Arbitrary constant-vector tensors reduce locally to finitely many basis coordinates, compactness makes one finite coordinate set, and AC supplies the basis. Empty support/open/closed subspaces, zero coefficients, finite sums, and compact X checked. Reader sign, annulus, tensor and source-locator repairs accepted.
